Weave & Construction.name: Ottu (Single Warp) Weave
Weave & Construction.description: The simplest Kanjeevaram construction. The border is woven separately and joined to the body using the 'petni' interlock technique. Lighter in weight than double-warp sarees, making it more comfortable for everyday draping.
Weave & Construction.notes: Good entry point for first-time Kanjeevaram buyers due to lighter weight and lower cost.

Weave & Construction.name: Korvai (Rettapet)
Weave & Construction.description: The signature Kanjeevaram technique. Body, border, and pallu are each woven on separate warps with separate shuttles, then interlocked at the join so the colours can differ dramatically — for example a maroon body with a green border — while the seam stays almost invisible from the front.
Weave & Construction.materials: Pure mulberry silk, contrast-colour zari borders
Weave & Construction.notes: The interlocking join is the technical signature that distinguishes genuine Kanjeevaram weaving from printed or power-loom imitations.

Weave & Construction.name: Double Warp Weave
Weave & Construction.description: Uses two sets of warp threads twisted together, producing a denser, heavier fabric with more drape and durability. This is what gives classic Kanjeevarams their characteristic stiffness and longevity — heirloom sarees passed down generations are usually double-warp.
Weave & Construction.materials: Double mulberry silk warp threads, gold/silver zari
Weave & Construction.notes: Heavier on the body but far more durable; often the choice for sarees meant to last decades.

Motif & Design Tradition.name: Temple Border (Gopuram)
Motif & Design Tradition.description: A zigzag or stepped border pattern that echoes the stepped towers (gopurams) of South Indian temple architecture. One of the oldest and most recognisable Kanjeevaram border designs.
Motif & Design Tradition.materials: Silk with wide zari temple-pattern border
Motif & Design Tradition.notes: Considered the most traditional and auspicious border style, closely tied to Tamil temple culture.

Motif & Design Tradition.name: Checked / Rudraksha Border
Motif & Design Tradition.description: Small bead-like motifs, resembling rudraksha seeds, repeat along the border in a continuous row, giving a textured, devotional look.
Motif & Design Tradition.notes: Often paired with plain or lightly-worked bodies to keep the focus on the border detail.

Motif & Design Tradition.name: Vairaoosi Border
Motif & Design Tradition.description: A repeating diamond-shaped pattern woven along the border, named after 'vairam' (diamond). The geometric repetition gives a sharp, structured edge to the saree.
Motif & Design Tradition.notes: A popular alternative to temple borders for those who prefer a more geometric, modern look while staying traditional.

Motif & Design Tradition.name: Peacock (Mayil) Motif
Motif & Design Tradition.description: Peacocks — a recurring symbol in Tamil art and temple sculpture — are woven into the pallu or scattered across the body, often facing each other in pairs.
Motif & Design Tradition.materials: Silk, zari peacock motifs on pallu/body
Motif & Design Tradition.notes: One of the most sought-after motifs for bridal trousseaus.

Motif & Design Tradition.name: Yaali / Simha Motif
Motif & Design Tradition.description: Mythical lion-like creatures (yaali) drawn directly from South Indian temple pillar sculpture, woven into the pallu as guardian figures.
Motif & Design Tradition.notes: Considered a heavier, more elaborate motif reserved for grand occasions.

Motif & Design Tradition.name: Rudraksham Motif
Motif & Design Tradition.description: Small rudraksha-bead-inspired motifs are scattered across the body rather than confined to the border, giving an all-over devotional texture.
Motif & Design Tradition.notes: Distinct from the rudraksha border style since the motif covers the full body, not just the edge.

Motif & Design Tradition.name: Kuyil Kann (Koel's Eye) Motif
Motif & Design Tradition.description: A small teardrop or eye-shaped motif named after the koel bird's eye, usually repeated in rows across the body as a subtle all-over texture.
Motif & Design Tradition.notes: A more understated motif, popular for sarees meant for regular festive wear rather than bridal use.

Motif & Design Tradition.name: Mango (Mangai) Motif
Motif & Design Tradition.description: The paisley-like mango motif, a staple across Indian textile traditions, appears on the pallu or as a scattered body motif in Kanjeevarams.
Motif & Design Tradition.notes: One of the most versatile motifs, found across many weaving centres beyond Kanchipuram too.

Motif & Design Tradition.name: Checks and Stripes (Pattu Chex)
Motif & Design Tradition.description: Simple geometric checks or stripes woven across the body with minimal zari work, designed for comfort and understated elegance in daily or office settings.
Motif & Design Tradition.notes: The most affordable and lightweight category, often chosen for regular wear rather than special occasions.

Zari & Finish.name: Pure Zari (Real Gold/Silver Thread)
Zari & Finish.description: Woven with genuine gold or silver-coated thread, these are the most valuable and heaviest Kanjeevarams, typically reserved for weddings and passed down as heirlooms.
Zari & Finish.notes: Significantly more expensive; often purchased as an investment piece as much as an item of clothing.

Zari & Finish.name: Tested / Half-Fine Zari
Zari & Finish.description: Uses silver-coated copper thread instead of pure gold/silver, offering the look of traditional zari at a more accessible price point.
Zari & Finish.notes: The most common mid-range choice for buyers wanting an authentic look without bridal-level cost.

Zari & Finish.name: Art Silk Zari
Zari & Finish.description: Uses synthetic zari and often blended silk, making it the most budget-friendly Kanjeevaram-style saree, common in mass-market retail.
Zari & Finish.notes: Not considered a 'true' handloom Kanjeevaram by purists, but widely sold under the name for affordability.

Special & Heavier Categories.name: Bridal Kanjeevaram
Special & Heavier Categories.description: The heaviest and most elaborate category, combining dense pure zari work, contrast korvai borders, and a richly worked pallu. Often the centrepiece of a bride's trousseau.
Special & Heavier Categories.materials: Pure silk, heavy real/tested zari, korvai border
Special & Heavier Categories.notes: Can weigh significantly more than everyday sarees due to the density of zari work.

Special & Heavier Categories.name: Tissue Kanjeevaram
Special & Heavier Categories.description: A fine gold or silver thread is woven through the body of the silk itself, giving the fabric a shimmering, almost translucent sheen distinct from standard zari-bordered designs.
Special & Heavier Categories.materials: Silk with gold/silver thread woven through body
Special & Heavier Categories.notes: Prized for its shimmer effect, which changes appearance depending on light and draping.

Special & Heavier Categories.name: Bhutta / Butta Work
Special & Heavier Categories.description: Small individual motifs (buttas) are woven one at a time and scattered evenly across the body of the saree, each requiring separate shuttle work.
Special & Heavier Categories.notes: Labour-intensive since each motif is woven individually rather than as a continuous pattern.
